3	This document is a faithful conversion of the authoritative documentation

7	- AIRSS documentation (airss-docs.github.io): buildcell manual, utilities,

9	- C. J. Pickard and R. J. Needs, "Ab initio random structure searching",
10	  J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 23, 053201 (2011), and Phys. Rev. Lett. 97,
11	  045504 (2006).
12	
13	## Purpose of the format
14	
15	The `.res" file is the crystal structure input/output format of the SHELX
16	program suite. After each refinement cycle SHELXL (re)writes `name.res`;
17	it is similar to the input `name.ins` but carries the updated values of all
18	refined parameters, and it may be copied or edited into the `.ins` file for
19	the next refinement run. The AIRSS structure-prediction package stores its
20	resulting structures in SHELX-format `.res` files and converts between
21	`.res` and other formats with its `cabal` utility, so `.res` files
22	routinely travel between independently written programs.

    for raw in text.splitlines():

All checks pass. Here's a summary of the work:

## Root cause

The `.res` format specifies that an atom record's second field is the **scattering factor number** — the 1-based index of the atom's species in the file's own `SFAC` list (`paper.md`, "SFAC"/"Atom records"). The writer in `source/pymatgen/io/res.py` violated this in two ways:

1. **`ResWriter._ions_from_sites` wrote a running site counter** (`i += 1` → 1, 2, 3, … N) into the `sfac` field instead of the species' position in the SFAC list. For any structure with a repeated species (i.e. fewer species than atom records) the references either point at the wrong species or past the end of the list — exactly the `('O', 4), ('O', 5)` / `('Sr', 1, 'O')` failures reported.
2. **`ResSFAC.species` was an unordered `set`**, so the order of the SFAC line — which *defines* the numbering — was arbitrary and hash-seed dependent. The parser likewise collapsed the file's SFAC order into a set, so re-writing a parsed file destroyed that file's own numbering (demonstrated: `SFAC Si Cu Na Fe H …` differing on every run).

The round trip still passed because the library's own reader takes the species from the atom record's *label* and ignores the number — so the corruption was invisible to it, but fatal to any conforming external tool.

I also found a latent defect on the same code path: the label was formatted with an `s` format spec applied to the species object, which raises `TypeError: unsupported format string passed to Species.__format__` for oxidation-state decorated structures (export crashed), and a label longer than 6 characters ran into the species number, producing an unparseable record.

## Fix (`source/pymatgen/io/res.py`)

- `ResWriter._species_and_ions_from_sites` now builds the ordered species list and the atom records **together**: each distinct species label is collected once in order of first appearance, and every atom record references its own species' 1-based position — so references always resolve, for any composition, any number of species/sites, ordered or partially occupied sites, and with spin columns. Order of first appearance makes the export deterministic (`_ions_from_sites`/`_sfac_from_sites` kept as thin wrappers).
- `ResSFAC.species` is now a documented **ordered `list[str]`**, and the parser preserves the order read from the file, so read→write keeps a file's species list and references mutually consistent (bonus: `AirssProvider.as_dict()` is now JSON-serializable; a `set` was not).
- `Ion.__str__` renders the label with `!s` (identical to the string placed in the SFAC list, and works for `str`/`Element`/`Species`/`DummySpecies`) and always emits a separator before the species number. Column layout is byte-identical to before for labels up to 6 characters.

Nothing is keyed to a particular structure, species set, or ordering.

- `python reproduce.py` → `post_fix_success`, exit 0 (both checks pass).
